verdict.label: separate
verdict.why: onPointerDown and onPointerUp are complementary handlers of the same state machine: down sets up touch scroll, mouse reporting, link activation and selection state, and up tears it down and dispatches. Shared elements are only generic syntax (pointerType checks, preventDefault, and setPointerCapture vs releasePointerCapture, which are opposite operations), plus calls to existing helpers such as shouldReportTerminalMouse, sendMouse and linkAt. The handlers run different steps in different order. The only repeated fragment is a guarded release of pointer capture, and that is too small to justify a shared helper.
